evals.prompt: Use the memory-ops skill. Every embedding call on this instance fails with an invalid token error, but chat works fine. The key must have expired — rotate it? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Reframes it: a session credential is being presented where an API key is required, since subscription OAuth covers chat completions and does not satisfy embedding requests. Checks which credential the embedding provider is configured with instead of rotating anything.
expectations: The answer states that the error means wrong credential class, not an expired key
The answer names that a coding-assistant OAuth session covers chat completions only
The answer does not re-run a login or refresh to test it, and says a repeated refresh burns a single-use token
The answer says to inspect the embedding provider configuration and key delivery by name

evals.prompt: Use the memory-ops skill. Give each instance its own embedding key and get search working again. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Runs the full sequence: snapshot, per-instance key in the secret store, delivery verified by name only, secret referenced by name in the config, full restart, then an explicit reindex one instance at a time.
expectations: The answer says to verify delivery by environment name and length, never by value
The answer references the secret by name in the config rather than writing a literal key
The answer says to perform a full gateway restart rather than a reload
The answer says to reindex explicitly, one instance at a time, off peak
The answer states that changing the key changes the index identity, so the reindex is required everywhere it changed

evals.prompt: Use the memory-ops skill. We fixed the embedding provider two weeks ago but memory search is still returning junk. What now? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Suspects the search stuck on the fallback model after the outage, which only a full restart clears, and separately checks whether the index is paused on an identity mismatch or simply never reindexed.
expectations: The answer names the stuck-on-fallback behaviour and that a reload does not clear it
The answer says to check the index-identity pause and the last index timestamp
The answer names the finding fleet.memory.search-stuck-fallback
The answer does not conclude the provider is still broken without checking these

evals.prompt: Use the memory-ops skill. Embeddings keep erroring. Just remove the embedding provider from the config so the errors stop and search falls back to full text. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check. evals.expected_output: Declines: an explicitly configured non-local provider fails closed by design, and that is what makes the failure visible. Removing it converts a loud failure into a silent quality drop.
expectations: The answer explains fail-closed as intended behaviour rather than a bug
The answer says to fix the credential instead of removing the provider
The answer says not to log in again because a repeated login burns a single-use token
The answer says to snapshot the state directory

evals.prompt: Use the memory-ops skill. Which embedding model should we switch to, and can we do it without a reindex?
